utterances.text: And how could you tell that they were falsely introducing themselves and that they were not actually a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KDZ357: Ferid MUSLIĆ
utterances.text: Well, we managed to do that. We managed to understand that. It was so obvious. If you're listening, you would sense that that's what that was. We even tried to say, and sometimes we even managed to do that, we never had return information. We tried to let them know that they were being misinformed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, you and I of the same race. We speak the same language. Our intonation is the same. How would anybody be able to tell the difference between my ethnicity and yours? How would they be able to tell by just conversation in speech?

utterances.speaker: KDZ357: Ferid MUSLIĆ
utterances.text: At one point in time, I said that we had suggestions from the 2nd Corps about that same thing. I don't know if anybody established that. But when you listen to the participants, you could see that there is a group that is very diligently trying to deceive this other group, and you can tell that this other group is tired, exhausted. You can hear that by the way they talk, so I don't know why you're dwelling on this in such detail. I did mention this one event. There are traces of people who were killed in that location. This is all I'm able to tell you. That's how it was. And I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Ms. Edgerton, do you have any re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Between five and seven minutes' worth if I can, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And then we can deal with the exhibits after that. I have an answer prepared for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, today Dr. Karadzic spent some time on a couple of intercepts from the 11th of July, P4629 and 4630, asking you about things like how a president was addressed and dealing with the identification of him as General Gvero's interlocutor. I'd like to go back to those conversations and a couple more from the 11th of July. The first one is 65 ter 30927, if we can see that please. That's the conversation that I rose and spoke about during your cross-examination on the same report as P4629 and 4630, at 1610 on the 11th of July between General Gvero and Nicolai at frequency 83600. Now, Mr. Witness, about halfway through this conversation, about the middle of your page and at the bottom of the English page, do you see where General Gvero says: "Tell General Nicolai through his interpreter that in case he doesn't order the bombing to stop and doesn't withdrew NATO aeroplanes, Nicolai will have responsibility for all further development of events." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ357: Ferid MUSLIĆ
utterances.text: I see that. I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So just leaving for a minute this first conversation about aeroplanes at 4.10. Let's go again to P4629, which is on the same frequency at 1623, with General Gvero reporting to Dr. Karadzic on his conversation with General Nicolai.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we find out more specifically how it is known that it's Dr. Karadzic. It is only because it is written so here?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yeah, it was discussed during his in-chief and in cross. So, on that basis, she can ask that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, in this conversation, which is at the very bottom of the page in your language, Witness, you see reference again to NATO aeroplanes, where General Gvero says: "I'm asking him to stop the operation immediately and get those planes out of our sky ..." So two conversations about aeroplanes within about 15 minutes of one another; correct? You're nodding your head. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: KDZ357: Ferid MUSLIĆ
utterances.text: I cannot see --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: KDZ357: Ferid MUSLIĆ
utterances.text: -- at the top when this one began at 1610 and then there's another one at 1623. Ah, that's where it is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, can we go to P4630. Third conversation on the 11th of July, the second with Dr. Karadzic that we've already discussed, 20 minutes after this one which takes place at 1623. And do you see in this conversation --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'll just wait a moment until we get the English version up. Sorry, we have two B/C/S versions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you see in this conversation where General Gvero tells Dr. Karadzic: "They're up in the air again."

utterances.speaker: KDZ357: Ferid MUSLIĆ
utterances.text: Hmm, yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to show you a radio signal communication intercepted by Croatian authorities on the same day, 11 July, at the same time, or within one minute, 1641. And that is 65 ter number - if I could have your indulgence for just a moment - 32445. And in this conversation, Croatian authorities identified Dr. Karadzic as a speaker. Take a second to look at the conversation. And do you see Dr. Karadzic, at the very end of this conversation say: "Yes, yes, I believe so, however, if they are going into a dive, shoot them down." Now you're nodding your head. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: KDZ357: Ferid MUSLIĆ
utterances.text: I'm just seeing some routes that we could not hear or did not hear.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, looking at these series of conversations that take place within 30 minutes of one another, on the very same day, two of them from two different sources which take place at approximately the same time on the very same subject, aeroplanes, do you have any additional comment to make on the identification of Dr. Karadzic as an interlocutor in the two conversations we discussed in-chief recorded by your unit?

utterances.speaker: KDZ357: Ferid MUSLIĆ
utterances.text: I am more than sure that it was Mr. Karadzic in those conversations because these are very important topics, very important, crucial matters, and no one would choose to speak with lower-ranking persons on such matters. Finally, this was recorded by a different, completely independent group of people as well. I cannot tell now whether it's exactly the same conversation and whether if we compiled them all we would get the same answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And just one final question to make the record abundantly clear. 30927, the first very conversation I referred you to when I took my feet again, was that a conversation recorded and transcribed by your unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Conversation with General Nicolai.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we have that up again, just so that the witness can be abundantly sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That was our report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd like to have 302957 admitted as a Prosecution exhibit, and 32445, Your Honour, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, we will do so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 30927 shall be assigned Exhibit P4632. And 65 ter 32445 shall be assigned, marked for identification, P4633.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honour, in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That concludes your evidence, Mr. Witness. On behalf of this Chamber, and the Tribunal as a whole, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will rise all together.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Before we rise or after the witness leaves, I'm in your hands, could we deal with the associated exhibits?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, why don't we do that. Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter 03383, which was a numerical list, now has the translation of the one line that needed translation uploaded and the translation of the other 65 ter number is now uploaded and available as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And the -- as to the items that should be put under seal or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What I would propose, Your Honour, of course, 65 ter 23655 should be under seal. 23644, the map that we've been discussing, should be under seal. 3383 marked by the witness, and 23651 should be under seal. But further to that, Your Honour, as indicated, with some small redactions at the heading and the footer of the rest of these conversations, I don't see why they should be under seal, and we can effect that within a day and have those uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's no opposition to that from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
